notes:
Summary: large FS firm evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane for customer-facing assistant and internal doc search. Primary decision criteria are: latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99 alignment), measurable SLA language for tail, predictable reserved GPU sizing and costs, and KMS/data residency controls.

Recent activity: 
- 2026-03-02: 45m call w/ CTO Leila Ahmed, AE Casey, SE Maya. Walked through dedicated capacity options and baseline latency profiles. CTO: "we need predictable tail latency under load". Fireflies: ff-20260302-arg-002.
- 2026-02-14: discovery call + initial perf ask (concurrency targets, token rates). Fireflies: ff-20260214-arg-001.
- 2026-02-25: sent pricing + draft SLO language (drive link). Follow-up with legal scheduled.

Use-case details and targets: 
- Primary: customer support assistant (multi-turn chat, streaming preferred). Secondary: reranking for search results (non-streaming batch inference).
- Traffic profile: diurnal enterprise load, peak 500 concurrent active chats, average session 1600 tokens/day, expected growth 2x in 9 months.
- Throughput requirement for POC: sustain 1200 requests/minute with 1-2 second per-response SLA for median; goal to bound p95 non-streaming generation <= 150ms for short completions (<128 tokens) and p95 streaming first-token <= 250ms, tail (p99) <= 800ms for streaming end-to-end under peak. Reranking: target p95 <= 80ms.

Latency SLO & measurement alignment notes: 
- Client vs server timing: Argonaut measures client-side end-to-end (DNS+TLS+client queue+server processing+response delivery). Redwood reports server-side inference time by default (server receive -> last-token emit). Customer requests: standardized trace_id on every request so both sides can correlate.
- Proposal: define two SLO metrics in contract: (1) Server-inference SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for the inference phase only; (2) End-to-end SLOs measured client-side but explicitly excluding cold TLS handshakes and initial DNS cache misses. Both measured on 24h rolling window with min sample size 10k requests/day for SLA validity.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: split SLOs for 'first-token latency' and 'full-response latency' for streaming routes. Contract language example requested: "p95 first-token <= 250ms; p95 last-token <= 700ms for sequences <=512 tokens, measured at server-side; client-end logs used to corroborate."
- Warm-up & tail: agree to exclude the first 6 hours after deploy/rollout from SLA measurements to avoid cold-cache artifacts. Canary windows will be used for rollouts.
- Measurement tooling & transparency: Argonaut needs access to per-route latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) in Console, plus raw request traces for 30 days. Also wants automatic alerts when p99 exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive 5-min windows.

Reserved GPU planning & throughput guarantees: 
- Initial estimate: H100-class reserved pool (mix of 4 H100 + 4 A100) to meet latency under bursty traffic; Redwood SE to run benchmarking with Argonaut model weights and quantization profiles.
- Autoscale: prefer soft-autoscale with guaranteed baseline throughput; credits for bursting beyond reserved capacity. Argonaut expects explicit formula: reserved_slots * max_concurrency_per_gpu -> predict RPS.
- POC ask: Redwood to run synthetic load tests mirroring 500 concurrent chats with KV cache patterns and show p50/p95/p99 per-route. Provide batch size and token-rate deltas used.

SLA & commercial negotiation points: 
- Argonaut wants latency SLOs tied to service credits (sliding scale) and clear measurement windows. Also require an option to escalate to dedicated account engineering within 2 hours of sustained SLO violation.
- Legal: KMS ownership and key rotation must be documented; data residency for EU customers (separate contract addendum).

Next milestone: engineering kickoff 2026-03-18 to instrument trace_ids, agree on sample corpus for perf tests, and schedule 2-week dedicated POC in us-east-1. Deliverables: perf report (histograms), recommended reserved GPU count, proposed SLA wording for contract addendum.

Notes & friction: 
- Argonaut's infra team is sensitive to differences between client-observed and server-reported latency; they insist on trace-level correlation.
- Procurement pushing for upper-bound on monthly committed spend; need clear model for reserved vs burst costs.
- Security team asked for SOC2 + KMS diagrams; ticket SEC-1147 opened.

Stubs & refs: pricing deck link, security QA spreadsheet, jira tickets INF-3492 (perf test), SEC-1147 (kms/legal).
